**Job Purpose:** Responsible for performing and monitoring reconciliations of contingent and off-balance sheet General Ledger accounts, ensuring the accuracy and completeness of balances between source systems and the General Ledger. The role supports effective financial control through the identification, investigation, escalation and resolution of reconciliation exceptions while maintaining compliance with internal policies and regulatory requirements.

**Principal Accountabilities:**

* Perform daily reconciliations between source applications, sub-ledgers and the General Ledger for assigned contingent and off-balance sheet accounts.
* Review and analyse reconciliation reports covering Trade Finance, Collections, loan commitments, undisbursed facilities and other designated contingent accounts.
* Identify and investigate reconciliation differences, unmatched entries, aged items, abnormal balances and other exceptions.
* Review transaction details, accounting entries, interfaces and audit trails to determine root causes of reconciliation breaks.
* Engage with Operations, Product and Technology teams to facilitate timely investigation and resolution of outstanding items.
* Maintain exception trackers and monitor progress until all issues are appropriately resolved and closed.
* Escalate significant, recurring or overdue reconciliation exceptions to management.
* Prepare daily, weekly and monthly reconciliation MIS, ageing analysis, trend reporting and management dashboards.
* Identify process improvement opportunities and recommend enhancements to controls, data quality and automation.
* Ensure compliance with Bank policies, accounting controls, audit requirements and applicable regulatory standards.

* Professional accounting qualification such as CA, CPA, ACCA or equivalent is preferred.
* 5–8 years of relevant experience in banking operations, Trade Finance, reconciliation, financial control, business analysis or systems/change delivery.
* Hands-on experience in application-to-General Ledger reconciliation, exception investigation and management reporting.
* Working knowledge of contingent and off-balance sheet accounts and Trade Finance products is preferred.
* Hands-on experience with DCR (Data Control Reconciliation) or a similar automated reconciliation platform is preferred.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities with the ability to investigate and resolve financial discrepancies.
* Good understanding of General Ledger reconciliation, accounting controls, exception ageing and balance substantiation.
* Advanced Microsoft Excel skills including PivotTables, lookups and data reconciliation techniques.
* Exposure to Power BI, Power Query, SQL or similar analytics tools would be advantageous.
* Strong communication, stakeholder management and attention to detail.
* Ability to work independently and manage multiple priorities within tight reporting deadlines.

**About us**
------------

The Institute of Making is a unique organisation that explores, celebrates, and investigates materials and processes through a wide range of activities. From large-scale public events to ground-breaking academic research projects, our diverse outputs and many audiences are united by a shared passion for materials and making. On a day-to-day basis, we bring together students and staff from across UCL, to provide a creative home in which to collaborate, innovate, contemplate and experience making from a wide range of disciplines. At the heart of the Institute of Making are our open-access facilities, which include multi-material workshops and the Materials Library.

The Institute of Making opened in Bloomsbury in 2013 with a workshop offering a broad range of tools and machinery for inducted members to use. The Materials Library is an ever-expanding repository of some of the most extraordinary materials on earth, including shape memory alloys and self-healing materials as well as some of the more ordinary materials that have also changed the world, like paper, beeswax, and copper. The Workshop and our Materials Library sit side-by-side, enabling users to experience first-hand the relationships between materials and tools that constitute processes of making. The space is also a stage for our expansive events programme and a home to a multitude of research projects.

The Institute of Making workshop team is responsible for establishing the safe and sustainable operation of the workshops and supporting our members in using the equipment and facilities across both the Bloomsbury and Stratford sites. The team’s main duties include supervising members’ access to the space, inducting new members, conducting tool trainings, advising members on design, materials, and processes, supporting the delivery of events, and contributing to the friendly, welcoming, imaginative, and open-minded atmosphere of the Institute of Making.

**About the role**
------------------

**Please note, this role is currently only available to UCL staff.**

The post holder will oversee the portfolio of workshop-based activities that take place within the Institute of Making at Stratford. They will manage the day-to-day running of the space and technicians from the broader Institute of Making team when they are working at the Stratford site. They will also take responsibility for the overall health and safety of the space in relation to equipment, staff, members, protocols, and training. They will also collaborate in the recruitment of the intern team, who are a key part of the Institute of Making staff community offering tool trainings, events assistance, and support to members on a part-time basis.

They will work closely with the Head of Workshops and lead on the continual improvement, monitoring and reviewing of the arrangements for the Bloomsbury workshop. They should ideally have a passion for materials and a knowledge of making methods, tools, and processes. An approachable, friendly attitude is essential, and the successful candidate must be comfortable interacting with a wide range of people. They will also work closely with the Head of Events & Communications to ensure the safety of any visitor or participant in any Bloomsbury workshop-based events.

The post holder will act as Departmental Safety Officer and attend and contribute to faculty and departmental safety meetings as directed by the Head of Workshops. Through their management of the site, they will provide a safe, inclusive, and engaging environment for our members. The successful candidate will lead in providing a high standard of support to all workshop users, taking timely action on feedback. They will ensure technicians and members are equipped with the skills and confidence to use the workshop and may provide technical instruction where appropriate.

This role designs, launches, and scales the regional logistics network, ensuring best-in-class cost, service, and delivery speed.

Operating as a core member of the regional leadership team, this role is the primary partner to the COO in-region. It translates global logistics strategy into scalable, high-performing operations and shapes key decisions based on regional realities, including cross-border customs flows, Arabic labeling, cash on delivery, and seasonal demand peaks such as Ramadan, Eid, and White Friday.

This is a hands-on leadership role combining strategy, execution, and team building during a critical scale-up phase.

**Job Expectations:**

### **Build and Own the MENA Supply Chain Setup**

  

* Lead the end-to-end setup of the MENA logistics network, including selection of the regional hub (for example a free zone warehouse in Dubai) and the set-up of an Arabic and bilingual labeling solution in the MENA warehouse.
* Define the flow model for the region: import and consolidation at the hub, in-country distribution, and cross-border linehaul to the other GCC markets and, over time, the wider MENA region.
* Ensure the initial setup is scalable, cost-efficient, and operationally robust.
* Ensure logistics is a proactive enabler of growth, not a constraint.

### **End-to-End Performance Ownership**

  

* Own regional logistics KPIs across (i) cost (transport, warehousing, handling, customs duties and fees), (ii) service levels (OTIF, delivery promise accuracy, first-attempt delivery, cash on delivery remittance accuracy), and (iii) speed (lead times, delivery SLAs by country and city tier).
* Drive trade-off decisions across transportation, warehousing, and inventory, including air versus sea inbound and hub versus in-country stock placement.
* Plan capacity and inventory for regional demand peaks (Ramadan, Eid, White Friday) and for summer heat constraints on temperature-sensitive products.
* Establish full visibility and control over performance drivers.

### **Strategic Partner to COO (Regional Translation and Feedback Loop)**

  

* Act as the go-to logistics counterpart to the COO in MENA.
* Translate global strategy into executable regional plans.
* Provide structured feedback to global teams on (i) market constraints, (ii) performance gaps, and (iii) optimization opportunities.
* Proactively challenge and refine global assumptions based on MENA realities, such as address quality, last-mile variability, and payment preferences.

### **Customs, Compliance and Regulatory Coordination**

You'll lead a team of five administrators and take charge of the subscription budget, quarterly planning and renewals. We give you real decision-making authority: only spend above the limit, headcount or key vendor changes, risk acceptance and company-wide changes go up for approval. Everything else is your call, within the boundaries set out under "Decision Rights".

**You'll take ownership of:**

This is a hands-on lead role. Roughly 30% of your time goes to people, planning and alignment, and 70% to hands-on work: complex changes, incident investigation, configuration reviews, automation. You set up routine work so that it runs without you.

**1. Team and quarterly planning**

* Lead five administrators: 1:1s, goals, feedback. Run hiring for approved positions and, when necessary, parting ways — the latter agreed with your manager.
* Organize work across time zones: open incidents are handed over in writing to a specific person, and inconvenient hours are shared fairly. Three time zones cover about 13 hours of the working day, but not 24/7: you decide what truly requires a night-time or weekend response.
* Every critical system has a primary administrator and a backup who knows how to restore it.
* Each quarter, bring a plan: goals, owners, a support buffer and a list of what did not make the cut. Base it on feedback from engineers, recurring incidents and the renewal calendar. At the end of the quarter, show what was done, what was not and why. If urgent work comes up mid-quarter, say what moves and at what cost.
* Prepare a monthly report for the area: service and support health, access status, subscription spend and optimization results, key risks and items that need a management decision.

**2. Identity and access reviews**

* The identity provider is the central point of access provisioning: SSO, phishing-resistant MFA, role-based groups, SCIM. Hiring, transfers and terminations are triggered from the HR system.
* You verify revocation in the application itself. Deactivating a user in the identity provider does not end active sessions or revoke API tokens, local accounts and guest access. Systems without SCIM have an owner for manual revocation, and you make sure it is done.
* Access review frequency depends on risk: privileged and financial systems quarterly, everything else every six months. The system owner decides on each access, revocation is confirmed in the target system, and every exception has a reason and an expiry date. Results are retained as audit evidence.

**3. Corporate services and developer support**

* **Zero Trust access and DNS:** Zero Trust for internal tools (access policies, secure web gateway, device posture) and DNS for corporate domains. Policy changes roll out to a limited group first, and the on-call engineer has a rollback procedure. WAF and the product perimeter stay with DevOps.
* **Cloud, corporate side:** Cloud SSO integrated with the identity provider, role assignments agreed with DevOps, sandbox accounts, spend in corporate accounts. Organization structure and production belong to DevOps.
* **Corporate messaging:** Apps and integrations, guests and external channels, retention policies. Before a bot is installed, you know what data it reads and who owns it.
* **Collaboration suite:** Mail, calendar and documents: sharing rules, third-party OAuth apps, SPF, DKIM and DMARC, data transfer at offboarding.
* **Ticketing and knowledge base:** Permissions, projects and spaces, SSO sign-in. The ticketing system is the team's work queue, the knowledge base holds documentation.
* **Workstations:** MDM: encryption, updates, security policies, shipping a laptop to another country with zero-touch setup.
* Build self-service for developers: standard access is requested via chat or a ticket, approved by the resource owner and granted automatically for a limited time.
* Set support priorities: major outages and security incidents first, then requests that block teams from working.
* Together with DevOps, define clear ownership boundaries and drive shared requests to resolution: a ticket is closed when the problem is solved for the user, not when it has been handed to another team.

**4. Subscriptions and costs**

* Maintain the SaaS registry: owner, cost, number of seats, actual usage, renewal date and the last day the order can still be changed.
* Review paid seats separately from access reviews. Once a month, reconcile paid seats against activity. Long inactivity is a reason to check with the owner, not to reclaim the seat automatically: there are break-glass accounts and tools that are only needed once a quarter.
* Plan each contract review backwards from the last day the order can be changed or the renewal cancelled. By that day, the volume is agreed, the negotiation position is ready and the vendor has been notified if required. Example: 80 editor seats are paid for, 30 are actively used — we go to the vendor with 35 and a question about the pricing tier.
* Find shadow IT through OAuth grants and corporate card spend. In corporate cloud accounts, analyze bill growth by account and service together with the resource owner. Measure savings against invoices, separating realized savings from those expected at the next renewal.

**5. AI and automation**

For you, AI is the normal way the whole team works. What we expect:

* First-line support in chat: answers from the knowledge base with source links, request classification and ticket creation, handing unclear cases to a human.
* Preparation of access reviews and license reviews: AI reconciles exports from the identity provider, the HR system and applications and produces a list of anomalies for an administrator to verify.
* Measure the impact: compare time before and after rollout, including the time spent reviewing and correcting errors.
* Set the rules: what data may be shared with a model and where only a human makes the decision. AI does not grant privileged access or reset MFA: an administrator does that, verifying the employee's identity before any MFA reset.
* The whole team knows how to use these tools, not just you.

* **Okta, in depth:** SSO, SCIM, lifecycle management, MFA policies, Workflows. You have implemented it or significantly restructured it, not just created users.

The successful candidate should be technically competent, capable of interpreting engineering drawings, coordinating with internal and external project teams, and independently troubleshooting AV systems to ensure successful project execution and handover.

* Ensure compliance with company quality standards and project-specific HSE requirements.

Orbitworks is hiring a Program Quality Engineer to own quality for assigned satellite programs from contract review through customer acceptance and delivery. You’ll translate customer requirements into a Program Quality Plan and work with Engineering, Programs, Supply Chain, and Assembly, Integration & Test (AIT) to make sure those requirements are met throughout design, procurement, cleanroom assembly, integration, and environmental testing.

This is a new, hands-on role reporting to the Director of Quality & Mission Assurance. You’ll build the tools and processes for program quality while applying them to active programs as Orbitworks moves from its first flight model to repeat satellite production.

### **What you’ll do**

* Build and maintain Program Quality Plans, requirements flow-down matrices, phase-gate checklists, quality status reports, and delivery data package templates.
* Review contracts, statements of work, and customer specifications. Translate quality requirements into verifiable criteria for engineering teams, production, inspection, and suppliers.
* Define quality criteria and provide sign-off at design, test readiness, pre-shipment, and delivery reviews. Review acceptance test procedures and results, and approve delivery data packages and certificates of conformance.
* Serve as the customer’s primary quality contact. Lead customer acceptance reviews, source inspections, and audits, and communicate significant nonconformances and waivers as required by contract.
* Chair the program Material Review Board (MRB) and work with Engineering and Configuration Management to disposition nonconformances and manage deviations and waivers.
* Lead investigations into test anomalies, supplier escapes, and customer or audit findings. Agree on owners and deadlines, verify corrective action effectiveness, and escalate unresolved risks.
* Partner with Supply Chain and Supplier Quality on first article inspections, supplier corrective actions, and program-specific quality requirements.
* Report program quality risks and trends to leadership, and use lessons learned to improve quality processes across programs.

### **What you’ll bring**

* 6+ years in quality engineering for spacecraft, aerospace, or other high-reliability hardware, with an engineering degree or equivalent practical experience.
* Direct, hands-on experience supporting satellite or spacecraft hardware through assembly, integration, test, or delivery.
* Program-level quality ownership, including MRB decision authority and accountability for customer acceptance.
* Experience building and implementing a Program Quality Plan, process, or toolkit from scratch.
* Ability to interpret contracts, specifications, and engineering drawings and translate them into verifiable requirements for internal teams and suppliers.
* Experience dispositioning nonconformances, leading root cause investigations using methods such as 8D, 5 Whys, or Ishikawa, and verifying the effectiveness of corrective actions.
* Working knowledge of AS9100D, AS9102 First Article Inspection, and space hardware workmanship standards such as IPC J-STD-001 and IPC-A-610 space addenda, or equivalent. Exposure to ECSS or NASA quality requirements.
* Understanding of qualification and acceptance testing, including vibration, thermal vacuum, and electromagnetic compatibility testing.
* Clear technical communication in English and the ability to secure commitments across teams, suppliers, and customers without direct reporting authority.
* Ability to work onsite in KEZAD, including in the cleanroom and on the AIT floor, travel to suppliers, and meet applicable export-control requirements for program data access.

### **Nice to have**

* Experience moving small satellite or low Earth orbit constellation programs from first units into repeat production.
* Experience with ISO Class 8 or cleaner environments, electrostatic discharge controls, foreign object debris prevention, and contamination control.
* Experience leading spacecraft customer acceptance reviews, source inspections, supplier audits, or flight hardware deliveries.
* Experience with design and process FMEA, control plans, APQP, Lean, or Six Sigma.
* Experience using Jira, Confluence, Arena PLM, or similar tools to manage nonconformances, corrective actions, risks, and configuration records.
* ASQ CQE or CQA, AS9100 Lead Auditor, or IPC space addendum certification.

**About the role:**

Responsible to serve as the source of truth about passengers, who they are, what they value and where they struggle to ensure that design, investment and operational decisions across HIA are based on evidence. Own end-to-end Voice of Customer programme, from data collection and research through to insight generation and strategic dissemination, ensuring every major capex, technology, and service-design decision is backed by robust passenger evidence, reducing wasted spend and improving the return on every investment in the airport, to ensure HIA is a customer-centric airport.

**Key responsibilities**

**Strategic**

* Define and evolve the VoC strategy across all HIA touchpoints (landside, airside, retail, lounge, transfer, arrivals), aligning measurement frameworks with MATAR's wider CX Strategy & Roadmap and commercial objectives, to ensure passenger insight remains central to long-term planning.
* Design and maintain passenger segmentation models, personas, and end-to-end journey maps (e.g., premium, family, PRM, transfer, O&D) so that CX initiatives, capital projects, and commercial offers are targeted to clearly defined passenger needs rather than assumptions.
* Develop and present executive-level insight packs (with clear "so-what" narratives and prioritised recommendations) for APC, the CX & Brand Committee, and project steering groups, to embed passenger evidence into investment cases and governance decisions.

**Operational**

* Establish an insight-led decision-making culture by implementing a policy requiring all major design, technology, and capex proposals to reference VoC data, reducing the volume of "unknown" or anecdotal decisions across the organization.
* Partner with Qatar Airways (QR), Qatar Duty Free (QDF), and Qatar Aviation Services (QAS) analytics teams to link passenger satisfaction insights with loyalty, dwell-time, and commercial-spend data, enabling a unified view of passenger value and behavior across the airport ecosystem.
* Benchmark HIA's VoC programme against global best practice (Skytrax, ACI ASQ, and leading hub airports) to identify emerging methodologies, technologies, and standards, ensuring HIA maintains its competitive edge in passenger experience measurement.
* Identify and prioritise passenger pain points and opportunity areas through root-cause analysis and trend monitoring and translate these into a prioritised improvement backlog that informs the CX Roadmap and annual business planning cycle.
* Champion data governance and ethical research standards across all VoC activities, ensuring compliance with Qatar data-protection regulations and international best practice for passenger privacy, consent, and data security.
* Own and operate the integrated VoC collection ecosystem - including CSAT/NPS surveys, SMS and QR code intercepts, digital feedback channels, social-media listening, and complaint/compliment analysis - to maximise coverage and response rates at every key passenger touchpoint.
* Commission and conduct targeted qualitative research (ethnographic studies, passenger interviews, journey shadowing, mystery shopping, and UX testing) to uncover deep behavioral insights that quantitative data alone cannot reveal.
* Manage closed-loop feedback processes by routing actionable alerts to relevant operational teams (e.g., facilities, operations, security), tracking resolution, and reporting back to passengers where appropriate, to demonstrate that feedback drives tangible change.
* Administer and optimize VoC technology platforms (e.g., survey tools, text/sentiment analytics, dashboards) to ensure data accuracy, system reliability, and integration with business-intelligence infrastructure.
* Coordinate fieldwork logistics for passenger intercept surveys, pop-up research, and observational studies across the terminal, working with airport operations and security to ensure research activities do not disrupt passenger flow or operational efficiency.
* Produce ad-hoc insight briefings and rapid-turnaround analyses in response to emerging issues (e.g., disruption events, new facility openings, seasonal peaks), equipping leadership with real-time passenger sentiment to guide immediate decisions.
* Manage external research vendors and agency relationships, including scope definition, procurement, quality assurance, and budget control, to ensure third-party deliverables meet HIA's standards for rigor and relevance.
* Build internal VoC capability by training and coaching cross-functional stakeholders (project managers, operational leads, commercial teams) on how to interpret and apply passenger insights in their day-to-day decision-making.
* Maintain a centralized insights repository that is accessible to authorized stakeholders, ensuring historical data, research reports, and persona documentation are well-organised, version-controlled, and easily retrievable.
* Perform other department duties related to his / her position as directed by the Head of the Department

Technical and Commercial

* 10+ years construction commercial or quantity surveying experience, contractor side or main contractor commercial team.
* Deep working knowledge of IPC cycles, BOQ, cost value reconciliation, CPI and EAC mechanics, and WIP first principles, including the distinction between disputed and uncertified but complete.

* Demonstrable track record of improving WIP, collections, or cash positions, not just reporting on them.

* [AI] Ability to articulate a clear vision for how AI changes what a commercial function can achieve, specifically in preventing cash flow leakage and accelerating resolution of commercial issues.

Personality and Working Style

**Job Summary**

Lead independent fire and life safety design assurance for Qiddiya City assets across masterplan, concept, detailed design, construction and handover. The role verifies that fire strategies, drawings, calculations and specifications satisfy Saudi Building Code, Saudi Civil Defense requirements, applicable NFPA standards and Qiddiya operational requirements, while ensuring proposed solutions are practical to operate, maintain and respond to during emergencies.

**Responsibilities**

**Core Responsibilities**

* Lead risk-based reviews of fire strategies, code analyses, drawings, specifications and technical submissions at each design gateway.
* Verify means of egress, occupancy, fire resistance, compartmentation, fire stopping, smoke control, fire detection and alarm, suppression, fire water, firefighting access and emergency power provisions.
* Review performance-based and alternative solutions, including fire and evacuation modelling assumptions, acceptance criteria, sensitivity analyses and proposed compensatory measures.
* Review fire alarm zoning, cause-and-effect matrices, emergency voice communication, interfaces with BMS/CCU and the integrity of life-safety signalling architecture.
* Record clear, traceable comments with code references, risk significance, disposition and closure evidence using approved document-control systems.
* Coordinate multidisciplinary reviews with architecture, structure, MEP, security, accessibility, transport, operations, venue and emergency-response stakeholders.
* Identify operational, maintainability and emergency-response risks early and ensure these requirements are incorporated into design briefs and employer requirements.
* Support technical workshops, design review meetings and engagement with Saudi Civil Defense, third-party reviewers and authorities having jurisdiction.

**Specific Responsibilities**

* Maintain a design assurance register and report overdue, repeated or high-risk design issues to FLS leadership.
* Assess design changes, value-engineering proposals, deviations and waivers for life-safety impact before acceptance.
* Support commissioning, integrated testing and handover teams by translating design intent into verifiable acceptance criteria.
* Undertake targeted site inspections to confirm installed works remain aligned with approved design and fire strategy.
* Provide technical mentoring to engineers and contribute to standards, design guides, lessons learned and Saudization initiatives.

**Generic Responsibilities**

* Comply with Qiddiya governance, confidentiality, HSE, information-management and delegated-authority requirements.
* Prepare concise technical reports, dashboards and management briefings; manage priorities and deliverables to agreed dates.
* Promote collaboration, professional challenge, continuous improvement and a life-safety-first culture.

**Key Internal Interactions**

* City Operations FLS; Development and Delivery; Asset Management; Engineering; HSE; Security; CCU; Digital/ICT; Procurement; Legal; venue and asset operators.

**Key External Interactions**

* Saudi Civil Defense and other authorities having jurisdiction.
* Design consultants, fire engineers, architects, MEP engineers, contractors, specialist vendors, commissioning agents and third-party certifiers.

 **Requirements**

* Bachelor degree in Fire Engineering, Fire Safety Engineering, Mechanical/Electrical Engineering, Building Services or a closely related discipline.
* Postgraduate qualification in fire engineering or life-safety design is desirable.
* Professional membership of IFE, SFPE, CIBSE or equivalent; chartered or professional registration preferred.
* Relevant Saudi Council of Engineers registration where applicable.
* Strong application of SBC 201 and SBC 801, Saudi Civil Defense requirements, NFPA 1, 13, 20, 72, 92, 101 and relevant IBC/IFC provisions.
* Fire strategy review, egress analysis, smoke-control assessment, system interface review and evidence-based technical writing.
* Ability to interpret drawings, BIM outputs, calculations and technical specifications and to manage design comments to closure.

* Minimum 8 years of progressive fire and life safety design or assurance experience, including at least 3 years leading complex reviews.
* Design-consultancy, client-side assurance or authority-review experience on complex mixed-use, entertainment, transport, high-rise or major development projects.

* Saudi Arabia or GCC experience and interface with Saudi Civil Defense strongly preferred.

Bringing people together around a shared goal is how you advance risk posture across complex environments. Cybersecurity is a shared responsibility that no single team can carry alone, so the relationships you build matter as much as the controls you put in place. Working in close collaboration with IT, privacy, clinical, and corporate teams allows you to apply security controls in ways that support everyday work. Whether you are shaping a new policy or rolling out a control, you build support across teams by showing how it protects the work they already care about. The Retail Operations Leader sets and upholds national operating standards across our regular and outlet stores. Reporting to the Retail Experience and Enablement Leader, this role owns store SOPs and readiness, leads compliance reviews and audit follow-up, drives Tailorshop productivity and quality, and provides oversight of the service desk and store support functions. This is a field-facing role: approximately 50% of your time will be spent in stores, reviewing operations and supporting leaders in person, so regular travel across our national store network is required. The Retail Operations Leader is the first escalation point for store operations leaders and ensures every store works from one clear set of operating instructions.

**Responsibilities in this role:**
----------------------------------

**Set Standards and Readiness**

* Write and maintain SOPs for service desk, POS, returns, client files, Tailorshop and BOPIS; approve changes within national policy and submit new standards for approval.
* Release each SOP change to stores with a summary of what changed and the effective date, and review each SOP annually and after any audit finding.
* Build readiness checklists for peak periods, promotional events and inventory counts, and track store sign-off to confirm completion before each date.

**Drive Store Compliance**

* Spend up to 50% of your time in stores, visiting every regular and outlet location at least once per year.
* Set a compliance review schedule covering every store and complete reviews in store or remotely, checking service desk, POS, returns and client files against SOPs.
* Score each review, report results by store to the respective DVP, and log each corrective action with an owner and date, following up until closed.

**Lead Tailorshop Productivity**

* Write Tailorshop operating standards for intake and associated procedures, and own the Tailorshop tool for measuring productivity and quality.
* Report turnaround and quality by store monthly; escalate stores below standard to their DVP, investigate causes and propose solutions (e.g. outsourcing, productivity by tailor).
* Develop capacity planning strategies to manage peak demand while maintaining quality standards.
* Partner with Operations Leaders on best practices, training gaps and financial efficiency, and oversee technology and equipment upgrades.

**Own Governance and Loss Prevention Follow-Up**

* Update store LP protocols with the LP team when policy changes or an audit shows a gap, and build them into SOPs and compliance reviews.

* Investigate inventory count variances with LP and the Director of Logistics, Store Network, and report causes and fixes.

* Support onboarding of each new operations leader: share current SOPs, the compliance schedule and open audit actions, walk through their store’s results, and check in at 30, 60 and 90 days.
* Act as the first escalation point for SOP and procedure questions, updating SOPs when the same question recurs.
* Align with the Director of Logistics, Store Network before any operations change affecting store logistics roles, so stores receive one set of instructions.

**Lead Operations Communication**

* Run the weekly operations call: set the agenda, cover SOP changes, readiness dates and open audit actions, and publish actions after the call.
* Log store requests to central office teams, route each to an owner and track it to close.
* Oversee that the IT roadmap for operations-related store technology stays on track with updates, enhancements and timelines.

**Lead the Service Desk**

* Provide oversight for the service desk and store support functions, driving operational efficiencies across the chain.
* Establish service standards and processes that support elevated customer experiences and NPS objectives.
* Develop cross-functional workforce strategies to increase role versatility and optimize resources.
* Ensure compliance with chain-wide POS policies and lead inventory management initiatives that improve speed and accuracy.

The National Director, Employee and Labour Relations is a senior member of the CHRO's leadership team, providing strategic leadership for Bayshore's national employee and labour relations function. The Director leads and builds a national team of Employee and Labour Relations professionals — setting strategic direction, quality standards, and professional development plans that establish the function as a true centre of excellence.  
  
This role is accountable for proactively identifying employee and labour relations risk across the organization and designing the strategies, policies, and programs that mitigate that risk before it escalates — shifting Bayshore's ER/LR posture from reactive case management toward forward-looking risk management. A central pillar of this proactive strategy is building the capability of people leaders and HR Business Partners across the organization, so that sound employee relations practice is embedded at the point of leadership rather than escalated after the fact.  
  
A second, equally critical accountability is ensuring a harmonious union-management relationship and an effective national collective bargaining process.  
  
**Key Responsibilities**  
  
**Team Leadership & Strategic Direction**  

* Lead, build, and develop a national team of Employee and Labour Relations professionals, providing coaching, feedback, and career development that allows the team to grow in capability and operate as a centre of excellence.
* Serve as a key member of the CHRO's leadership team, participating in strategic and operational discussions on HR priorities, systems, performance indicators, and budgets.
* Own Bayshore's national employee and labour relations strategy, translating legislative, sector, and organizational risk trends into forward-looking policy and program design.

  
**Proactive Risk Identification & Mitigation**  

* Proactively scan for emerging employee and labour relations risk — legislative change, sector trends, union activity, and workplace culture signals — and translate findings into mitigation strategies before issues escalate into formal complaints or grievances.
* Establish leading-indicator reporting (grievance trends, complaint patterns, engagement signals, turnover hot spots) that allows the team and people leaders to intervene early, rather than respond only after a formal issue has surfaced.
* Design and continuously refine policies, guidelines, and programs that reduce organizational exposure to legal, reputational, and labour relations risk, with particular focus on inclusive and psychologically safe work environments.
* Establish governance and oversight for legal challenges (wrongful and/or unjust dismissal claims, Human Rights complaints) and grievances, ensuring risk is surfaced and addressed at the earliest possible stage.
* Identify integration points to embed diversity, inclusion, and accessibility goals proactively across the employee and labour relations strategy.

  
**Building Leader & HR Business Partner Capability**  

* Design and deliver a national capability-building curriculum for people leaders and HR Business Partners on employee relations fundamentals — productive performance management conversations, building trust, implementing corrective action, and resolving issues early.
* Build a scalable coaching model so HR Business Partners can confidently and independently manage low- and moderate-complexity ER matters, reserving specialist team involvement for high-risk or precedent-setting cases.
* Monitor leader and HR Business Partner capability maturity across the organization, using the data to prioritize where training investment will most reduce future employee and labour relations risk.
* Serve as an escalation point and expert advisor to HR Business Partners and Health & Safety Specialists on complex ER cases and the interpretation of collective agreements and relevant jurisprudence.

  
**Employee Relations Oversight**  

* Provide oversight of the team's conduct of sensitive, high-risk investigations (harassment, discrimination, hostile work environment, and unfair treatment complaints), ensuring rigor, consistency, and legal defensibility.
* Provide senior-level oversight of termination and complex employee relations cases, enabling HR Business Partners, Health & Safety Specialists, and Clinical Specialists to build the case, determine corrective measures, and support managers through delivery.
* Participate in the employee and labour relations dimensions of large-scale reorganization initiatives.
* Prepare executive briefings on employee and labour relations trends and risk exposure, with recommendations to close gaps — shifting reporting from incident-based updates toward proactive risk dashboards.
* Develop new policies and revise existing ones, incorporating the implications of HR legislative change across Canada and harmonization opportunities with emerging best practice.

  
**Labour Relations & Collective Bargaining**  

* Lead the organization's response to union certification drives and serve as a key participant in the collective bargaining process, advising senior management and engaging union officials on the interpretation and application of the collective agreement.
* Review and approve collective bargaining mandates and proposed terms, partnering with business leaders and HR Business Partners to ensure collective employment terms align with Bayshore's values and business strategy.
* Manage the national grievance process and educate management on negotiated contract changes, supporting implementation as required.
* Provide expert advice to HR Business Partners, Health & Safety Specialists, and management on the interpretation of the collective agreement and application of relevant jurisprudence in complex cases.

**WPHS Program Governance, Standards & Continuous Improvement**

* Lead IGM’s Workplace Health and Safety program for corporate campuses and supported IGWM and Mackenzie distribution locations across Canada, applying advanced knowledge of workplace health and safety, legislative requirements and market practices.
* Establish, maintain and improve policies, procedures, standards, tools, templates and governance routines to support consistent execution across jurisdictions.
* Manage third-party consultant support, including scope, cadence, deliverables, findings, benchmarking, recommendations and implementation follow-up.
* Use incident trends, inspection results, committee feedback, audit outcomes and industry practices to strengthen program maturity, controls and reporting.

**Legislative Compliance, By-Laws & Risk Management**

* Monitor applicable Canadian workplace health and safety requirements, including provincial legislation and relevant municipal by-laws, and translate obligations into practical operating standards.
* Identify workplace hazards, compliance gaps and emerging risks; support risk assessments; recommend corrective actions; and track remediation to completion.
* Collaborate with HR, Legal, Risk, Compliance, Facility Management, Security, Business Continuity, landlords, vendors and consultants to support regulatory readiness.
* Escalate sensitive, urgent or higher-risk matters with clear facts, options, recommendations and business impacts.

**Committees, Representatives & Internal Responsibility System**

* Support Joint Health and Safety Committees, health and safety representatives, fire wardens, first aiders and people leaders with guidance, templates, agenda support, issue tracking and escalation pathways.
* Reinforce shared accountability for safe work practices and the effective operation of the internal responsibility system across IGM’s portfolio.
* Clarify roles, responsibilities, expectations and decision paths to improve consistency and follow-through across sites.

**Incident, Hazard & Inspection Management**

* Oversee processes for reporting, documenting, investigating and following up on workplace incidents, hazards, inspections, employee concerns and corrective actions.
* Work closely with local leaders, Facility Management, HR, Legal, Risk, Security, Business Continuity, landlords, vendors and consultants to ensure timely response and practical resolution.
* Resolve difficult and sometimes complex matters by identifying root issues, evaluating alternatives and recommending new approaches where established processes do not fully address the issue.
* Track incidents, hazards, inspections and corrective actions through completion, identifying trends and recurring issues that require additional controls, communication, training or escalation.

**Training, Awareness & Communications**

* Coordinate mandatory workplace safety training, committee education, leader awareness, employee communications, emergency procedure awareness and targeted safety campaigns.
* Ensure materials are current, practical, accessible and aligned to workplace risks, legislative requirements, IGM values and business needs.
* Communicate clear guidance on policies, procedures and practices to employees, leaders, committees, consultants, vendors and senior stakeholders, particularly during sensitive or urgent matters.

**Reporting, Metrics & Performance Discipline**

* Develop and maintain reporting on incidents, hazards, inspections, training completion, committee effectiveness, corrective action status, emerging risks, consultant findings and program maturity.
* Use data, consultant recommendations, audit outcomes and lessons learned to improve controls, service standards and documentation.
* Apply sound judgment by prioritizing work, managing issue closure and recommending practical improvements that balance stakeholder experience, cost, risk, compliance and operational continuity.

* Manage scope, deliverables, cadence and performance of third-party workplace health and safety consultant services.
* Lead through influence by building productive relationships, clarifying accountabilities and maintaining timely, professional communication across matrixed teams and external partners.

* This role requires 3-5 days a week on site to support campus operations, committee activities, inspections, training, incident response, and stakeholder engagement.

At BlueCosmo, we keep people connected where cell coverage ends. From remote adventures to critical business operations, we provide satellite phones, messengers, and data solutions that help people stay connected when it matters most.

As a Roadpost brand, we partner with leading satellite networks, including Iridium and Inmarsat, and offer trusted products like ZOLEO. But we’re more than just a hardware retailer; our business is built on lasting subscriber relationships, with recurring airtime services at the heart of what we do.

**Why This Role Matters**

We sell satellite telephony — Iridium phones, Inmarsat handsets, GO devices, SIM cards, and airtime plans. AI handles the straightforward volume. What reaches you is the stuff that actually needs a human: a phone that won't connect in the field, a SIM that isn't provisioning, a customer who needs to be in the right plan before they fly out tomorrow. The problems that reach you are telephony-based — power, signal acquisition, dialing, SIM provisioning, airtime balances, number management, and device configuration.

Reporting to the MSS Team Lead, you own those issues start to finish, and you take the initiative to pick up what's next. The customers who contact us depend on their satellite device for continuity of communication — sometimes in genuinely remote or high-risk situations. That urgency is part of the job.

**What You’ll Do**

* **Ownership and continuity of communication.** This is the headline quality we hire for. Take the ticket, work it, close it. Customers in the field cannot afford gaps in coverage — that reality should drive how you prioritize. If you can't resolve something, you find out how. You take the lead on the next step rather than waiting for a manager to assign it, point you to a call, or explain what needs to be done. This role is a great fit for people who enjoy that kind of independence.
* **Product and service knowledge.** Know every product we sell and what it does: Iridium and Inmarsat satellite phones, Iridium GO, Beam and ASE docking stations, SIM cards, airtime plans, and the full range of antenna and cabling configurations. You're not selling; you're helping them land on the right answer. That means knowing our products well enough to give a confident, accurate recommendation without a script.
* **Self-direction and problem solving.** Box in the issue before you start solving it. Triage properly — eliminate what it isn't before you decide what it is. Use the web, manufacturer documentation, forums, and AI tools to find answers. Curiosity and a drive to learn are essential in this role. When a fix doesn't work, you try a new angle rather than repeating the same step. When you genuinely can't resolve something, you escalate with a full brief and still own the customer interaction to closure.
* **Working with AI.** You'll use AI every day — to research problems, find solutions, and learn faster. You'll also judge whether an AI response to a customer is actually right, and flag to our Optimization team when it isn't. When you spot a repeat issue across tickets that could be automated or handled without a human, you bring it forward. We want people who ask how this could be solved at the system level, because improving the AI's handling of common issues is part of how this team succeeds. That contribution is valued here.
* **Knowledge base contribution.** When you solve something new, or find that an existing article is wrong or missing, you document it. KB articles and updated SOPs are part of your output. The team's collective knowledge is only as good as what gets written down.
* **On-call rotation.** You'll rotate for after-hours emergencies and periodic weekend ticket handling alongside the rest of the team — a handful of incidents per month at most. These are real situations: a customer whose satellite phone stopped working the night before a remote expedition, or a vessel that's lost communications.

The incumbent is an entry-level front line supervisor position responsible for meeting CN's service commitments by managing the day-to-day train operations within a territory or terminal and the unionized train crews associated. **Role description:**

Join Arcadis’ Networking & Communications team as a Telecom Network Designer, helping clients plan, design, build, and manage fibre optic networks. Our work spans fibre optic networks of all types, from fibre-to-the-premises (FTTP), transport & back haul networks, subsea links, and intelligent transportation systems (ITS), combining practical outside plant design with GIS-based analysis and network asset management.

You’ll turn field information, network records, and project requirements into clear, accurate designs, cost estimates, and technical documentation. Working alongside senior technical staff and project managers, you’ll take ownership of assigned deliverables, coordinate with clients and contractors, and support projects from early planning through construction and through to operations. This role suits someone who enjoys working through design challenges, is comfortable with detailed data, and wants a mix of hands-on technical work and client collaboration across the full network lifecycle.

**Role accountabilities:**

Take responsibility for delivering conceptual, preliminary, and detailed fibre optic network designs across FTTP, transport and backhaul, and ITS projects. Develop practical, constructible solutions that address client requirements, site conditions, network performance, and future expansion. Document design decisions and assumptions, resolve technical issues within your scope, and bring forward matters requiring specialist input or professional review.

Use QGIS, IQGeo Network Manager Telecom, and COMSOF Fiber to prepare and analyse spatial data, develop network designs, and maintain reliable network records. Assess source information, identify gaps and inconsistencies, and establish a dependable data foundation for each assignment. Maintain traceable design files, revisions, and asset information through design, construction updates, and operational handover.

Plan and manage your technical work against agreed scope, milestones, and budgets. Coordinate inputs and dependencies, monitor progress, and communicate delivery status clearly to the project manager. Identify scope changes, missing information, and delivery risks early, explain their implications, and recommend a practical path forward.

Produce coordinated drawings, specifications, calculations, quantities, and technical reports that are accurate, consistent, and appropriate to the project stage. Check your work before submission, participate in peer reviews, and resolve review comments through to closure. Apply relevant codes, standards, client requirements, and Arcadis quality procedures, with clear documentation of assumptions and limitations.

Work directly with clients, contractors, vendors, and other design disciplines to confirm requirements, obtain information, and resolve technical questions. Explain design options and trade-offs clearly, assess proposed materials and equipment against project requirements, and follow technical actions through to resolution.

Plan and carry out site visits, surveys, and field assessments to verify existing conditions and inform design decisions. Respond to construction queries, assess proposed field changes, and review installation records and test results within the assigned scope. Reconcile field information and construction markups into accurate as-built drawings and network records.

Prepare material quantities, cost estimates, and technical inputs for project budgets and proposals. Develop clear estimating assumptions, compare design alternatives, and identify cost and constructability implications so clients and project teams can make informed decisions.

Deliver assigned technical services within managed service portfolios, including network record updates, troubleshooting, maintenance coordination, and underground locate program support. Improve repeatable workflows, templates, and data checks, and share practical knowledge that strengthens the consistency and efficiency of project delivery.

* Bachelor's degree (or equivalent) in Telecommunications Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related Engineering field.

* Registered and Active APEGA Membership with P.Eng or EIT status in the Province of Alberta.

* Professional credentials such as BICSI OSP or RCDD, or equivalent industry specific certifications.

* Additional technical training relevant to fiber optic outside plant design, GIS, or network design software.

* Advanced proficiency with GIS software (e.g., QGIS, IQGeo Network Manager Telecom, COMSOF AutoDesigner), CADD (2D/3D), AutoCAD, Revit, and advanced desktop applications.

### **About Sadie Restaurant**

Sadie is building voice AI for restaurants. Our voice AI host answers restaurant phones 24/7, takes reservations and takeout orders, and answers guest questions. It connects to the restaurant's reservation system and POS, so every call becomes a booking or an order and staff can stay focused on service.

We're looking for a bilingual (French and English) Customer Success Manager to get new restaurants live on Sadie and make sure they keep getting value after launch. You'll own each customer from kickoff through go-live and ongoing adoption. You'll plan the onboarding, coordinate setup and integrations, train managers and staff, and decide when a restaurant is ready to launch. After go-live, you'll watch usage and call performance and step in when adoption slips.

AI should be part of how you work. Use it to draft, research, analyze and automate parts of your workflow so you have more time for customers. You're responsible for the quality of the result.

### **What we value**

Following through on what you told a customer you'd do.

* Sound judgment when needs, priorities or timelines change.
* Staying calm when a customer is frustrated or the next step is unclear.
* Sharing context and asking questions openly.
* Questioning assumptions, including your own.

### **What you'll do**

**Get each restaurant live**

You're the main point of contact for new customers from kickoff through go-live. Take the handoff from Sales so you know the restaurant's goals, expectations, key contacts and implementation requirements. Build the onboarding plan with timelines, responsibilities, dependencies and go-live milestones, and keep communication clear and next steps agreed.

Gather and validate the restaurant information and workflows Sadie needs. Coordinate account setup, integrations with booking and point-of-sale (POS) systems, and configuration of Sadie's voice features, bringing in technical teams when you need them.

**Decide when a restaurant is ready to launch**

Before launch, coordinate checks of account setup, integrations and representative call scenarios, and track every issue through to resolution. Confirm the restaurant is ready, with setup complete, staff trained, launch expectations set and support routes clear.

The operator buys Sadie, but the guest is the one calling. Guests never chose Sadie and just want a table or an order. If the call goes badly, the restaurant wears it, so you don't sign off on a launch you aren't confident in.

**Train managers and staff**

Run virtual onboarding sessions and practical training for restaurant managers and staff, in French or English. Tailor each session to the team's needs and how comfortable they are with technology, so they feel confident on launch day.

**Build adoption after go-live**

Monitor usage, call performance and customer health to spot adoption gaps, emerging risks and chances to improve. Reach out with best practices, configuration recommendations and follow-up training before customers have to ask.

Stay a trusted advisor. Review progress against each customer's goals and help them get the most out of Sadie.

**Keep records and feed what you learn back to the team**

Work with Sales, Support and Product on handoffs, escalations and customer updates, with clear ownership and follow-through. Track onboarding timelines, go-live milestones, adoption and customer health, and tell the right people about progress and risks.

Keep clear customer records of goals, configuration decisions, onboarding progress, open issues and agreed next steps. Share customer insights, recurring problems and feedback with Product. Improve onboarding documentation, training materials and customer success playbooks so every restaurant gets a consistent experience as Sadie grows.

The Counsellor will work collaboratively with students, families, teachers, pastoral leaders and other professionals to deliver a proactive, developmentally appropriate and evidence-informed school counselling programme. The primary focus of this position is social and emotional counselling. Careers education, academic pathway guidance and university admissions are not core responsibilities of this role.

**Position Duties**
-------------------

The School Counsellor is responsible for and accountable for the following:

##### **Individual and group counselling**

* Provide developmentally appropriate individual and small-group counselling to support students' social, emotional and mental wellbeing.
* Support students experiencing anxiety, emotional distress, friendship difficulties, bereavement, adjustment difficulties and other personal challenges.
* Support students in developing self-awareness, emotional regulation, resilience, confidence, positive relationships and responsible decision-making.
* Identify students who may benefit from additional social and emotional support and implement appropriate early interventions.

* Support students whose social, emotional or mental health needs present barriers to engagement, attendance or learning.

* Support the development and implementation of appropriate individual student safety and support plans, in collaboration with relevant professionals.

**About the Role:**

As Domain Architect - AI Networking, you will be the primary technical authority for the physical and logical lifecycle of high-performance interconnect fabrics across a diverse portfolio of client environments, bridging the gap between architectural design and hands-on execution. You are a builder as much as an advisor: as comfortable configuring adaptive routing on a leaf-spine fabric from the CLI as you are explaining that configuration to a C-level audience.

As a global systems integrator, we don't simply operate static cloud environments. We design and deliver purpose-built, high-scale AI factories for some of the world's leading enterprises. In this role you will define the reference standard for network infrastructure, moving beyond single-switch administration to architect repeatable, scalable, and automated lossless fabrics. You will act as technical lead on NVIDIA Cloud Partner (NCP) and private enterprise AI cloud deployments, owning the network layer of the compute, network, and storage stack.

Your time will be split roughly 60/40 between delivering complex AI infrastructure (60%) and providing pre-sales subject matter expertise (40%). You will lead the physical provisioning of InfiniBand and Spectrum-X Ethernet fabrics for NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD, NVIDIA DGX BasePOD, and Cisco AI POD environments, ensuring clients inherit platforms that are genuinely ready for day-2 operations, while helping the sales team scope and cost future deployments.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Delivery and implementation**

**High-performance fabric design**

* Architect and deploy non-blocking fat-tree (Clos) topologies using NVIDIA Quantum-2 (NDR) and Quantum-3 (XDR) InfiniBand switches, and NVIDIA Spectrum-4 Ethernet switches.
* Implement rail-optimized network designs so GPU-to-GPU traffic aligns with compute-node PCIe topology, minimizing latency for NCCL collective operations.
* Configure adaptive routing, congestion control, and quality of service (QoS) to prevent head-of-line blocking and guarantee lossless data delivery. **In-network computing and offload strategy**
* InfiniBand: enable and tune SHARP (Scalable Hierarchical Aggregation and Reduction Protocol) on Quantum switches to offload collective operations (AllReduce, ReduceScatter) from the GPU to the switch silicon.
* Ethernet: architect high-performance Ethernet AI fabrics using SmartNIC/DPU offload (NVIDIA BlueField-3) to accelerate collective operations and isolate management traffic from the data path.
* Evaluate and roadmap emerging Ultra Ethernet Consortium (UEC) standards as the practice transitions in-network collectives from proprietary InfiniBand toward open Ethernet.
* Tune RoCEv2, PFC, and ECN on Ethernet fabrics and SmartNICs to approximate InfiniBand-class lossless behavior. **Fabric management, automation, and telemetry**
* Deploy NVIDIA UFM (Unified Fabric Manager) to manage InfiniBand subnets and NetQ for Ethernet fabric telemetry; implement PTP for nanosecond-level clock synchronization across the cluster.
* Use automation and AI-assisted tooling to generate switch configuration from the P2P cabling schedule, LLD, and PDG, then validate every topology in NVIDIA DSX Air before it ever touches hardware.
* Monitor fabric health continuously to identify slow receivers and link degradation in real time, and maintain Python and Ansible-based infrastructure-as-code for ongoing configuration management. **Layer 1 precision and performance engineering**
* Own the physical cabling strategy, defining cable schedules (DAC, AOC, or OSFP transceivers) that meet signal-integrity requirements over the required distances.
* Validate the link budget to ensure optical loss stays within acceptable limits for 400G and 800G links.
* Conduct acceptance and validation testing using NCCL tests to verify fabric performance against expected baselines.

**Pre-sales SME and consulting Technical scoping and estimation**

* Calculate the bisectional bandwidth required for a client's workload (for example, training typically requires 1:1 non-blocking; inference may tolerate 3:1 oversubscription), and produce accurate level-of-effort (LOE) estimates for statements of work.

**Bill of materials validation and architecture**

* Own the technical accuracy of the network bill of materials, validating that every switch, transceiver, and cable is on the NVIDIA or OEM hardware compatibility list (HCL).
* Manage the complexity of breakout cables (for example, 800G to 2x400G) and connector types (OSFP, QSFP112) to prevent on-site installation failures.

**Client workshops**

* Educate clients on the difference between standard enterprise Ethernet (lossy, TCP-based) and AI fabric (lossless, RDMA-based) traffic.
* Design the integration point between the high-speed “back-end” AI fabric and the client's existing “front-end” management network, including BGP/EVPN handoffs.

* Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
* Deep working knowledge of NVIDIA networking platforms, including Quantum InfiniBand switch architecture (MLNX-OS, UFM) and Spectrum-X Ethernet running NVIDIA Cumulus Linux or SONiC.
* Proficiency in RoCEv2 (RDMA over Converged Ethernet), including PFC and ECN, and a working architectural understanding of NVIDIA BlueField DPU and DOCA offload use cases.
* Automation and infrastructure-as-code experience, with proficiency in Python and Ansible for switch configuration management.

Agero is actively seeking **Remote Response Associates** to join our **Roadside Assistance** department, where you will help rescue stranded customers off the side of the road. When a vehicle breaks down, you are the driver's first point of contact. Taking real-time inbound calls from motorists across the U.S., you will be the calming voice that turns an unpredictable, highly stressful situation into a solved problem. You will provide a clear roadmap of what they can expect next, guiding them through an urgent and unplanned event. Just like an everyday superhero, you are stepping in to save their day and get their plans back on track!

As a **Remote Response Associate**, you serve as a lifeline for customers facing roadside emergencies such as flat tires, lockouts, dead batteries, fuel deliveries, and towing due to mechanical failures. Because customers often reach out feeling overwhelmed or unsafe on the side of the road, in dark parking lots, or while traveling in unfamiliar areas, you will manage these high-stress situations with calm, empathetic guidance and consistent reassurance.

Leading with a customer-first mindset, you will coordinate directly with external service providers to ensure the accurate and rapid dispatch of tow trucks and service vehicles. Your ability to stay calm and make quick decisions under pressure directly impacts customer safety, satisfaction, and our reputation for service excellence as a trusted, industry-leading roadside provider.

**Skills, Education, & Experience:** **What We're Looking For**

This isn't your typical, script-reading customer service role. We have a high bar for talent because our drivers need real help in real-time. To succeed here, you need to bring your A-game every shift, every call.

You don't just check a box or process a dispatch; you focus on the person behind the problem, ensuring both our customers and our roadside partners get high-quality, accurate, and timely support.
* **Tech Proficiency:** You are comfortable working with digital tools and fast-paced systems. You can confidently navigate online databases, CRMs, and complex dispatch software all at once. * **Accountability & Reliability:** Even in a remote environment, we hold our team to a high standard and operate a structured contact center with top-tier client expectations. select a dedicated production schedule with set days off. We require your consistent commitment to this schedule because a stranded driver is counting on you when you are on the clock. At the same time, due to the nature of our business, things move fast. Call volumes spike, schedules adjust, teams shift, and supervisors change - meaning you must be highly adaptable and ready to pivot.

**What this job is**

This is a broad operating leadership role. You will lead global infrastructure and Service Desk operations, develop a lean team, and get consistent results from our service providers. You need to stay close enough to the work to know where we have gaps, while making time to improve how the operation runs.

The operation is functioning, but too much time goes into reacting to issues. The opportunity is to strengthen ownership, follow through on commitments, and address the causes of recurring problems. We want an operation that responds well today and becomes more capable and self-managing over time.

You will lead from the front when needed, remove barriers, and help the team deliver with the people and partners we have. This requires both strategic judgment and personal engagement in service delivery. It is not a turnaround assignment or a mandate to rebuild everything.

We have distributed operations and significant reliance on managed service providers. We use modern Microsoft cloud services alongside business-critical legacy technology.

* Global responsibility for infrastructure, cloud operations, networking, end-user technology, Service Desk, IT service management, resilience, and the operational elements of cybersecurity.
* Support for major operating locations and small sales offices across time zones. Service standards need to be consistent while taking local business needs into account.
* Approximately 15 sites globally, including six in the US, four in Europe, and four in APAC. Europe includes two larger operating locations and two smaller sales offices; APAC includes India, China, Malaysia, and Singapore.

Your decisions will affect daily operations and customer service, from system availability and recovery to support quality, provisioning, and device management.

**Accountability for provider delivery**

Treat providers as part of the delivery team. Understand their scope, service performance, consumption, and invoices; handle escalations; and make informed recommendations about what to retain, renegotiate, replace, or bring in-house. You need to move comfortably between roadmap and budget decisions and daily delivery.

**Cost optimization and financial oversight**

You own cost optimization across the I&O domain. Understand what we are paying for, whether we are using it, and where we can reduce spend or get better value. Regular reviews and follow-through should be part of how the operation runs.

* Microsoft 365 licensing
* Azure optimization and oversight
* End-user tools and subscriptions
* Mobility and datacom
* Measurable results

**Experience and leadership expectations**

This role suits a director or a strong senior manager who has directly led infrastructure operations and a meaningful Service Desk or end-user support team. You should be comfortable leading eight people and using specialist providers as part of one operation.

**Relevant experience**

* Direct Service Desk leadership, including ticket governance, coverage, escalation, customer experience, knowledge management, endpoint provisioning, service metrics, and improvement.
* Infrastructure operating depth across Azure or comparable cloud services, Microsoft 365, identity, endpoints, enterprise networking, servers, monitoring, backup, patching, lifecycle management, and disaster recovery.
* Broad responsibility in a lean environment, with examples of improving uneven processes, technical debt, unclear ownership, or vendor performance.
* Global or multi-region operations, preferably across North America, EMEA, and APAC, with an understanding of regional coverage and local operating needs.
* Practical cost management across licensing, cloud consumption, subscriptions, mobility, or datacom, with measurable savings or better use of existing spend.

**What success looks like**

We should see reliable operations, responsive support, fewer recurring issues, and work followed through to completion. The team should be developing, providers should be delivering against clear expectations, and spend should be understood and actively managed.

The measure is an operation that becomes more effective and self-managing over time, with less operational noise and less need for daily CIO intervention.

Amazon Leo is building a low Earth orbit satellite broadband network to deliver fast, affordable connectivity to customers around the world, including those underserved by traditional infrastructure. We are looking for an experienced Incident Manager to serve as a Technical Call Leader. When a high severity event affects more than one part of the network, detection, customer communication, and engineering recovery are all happening at once, and someone has to run the whole event. That someone is you. You will be the single accountable owner of a high severity event from the moment it is declared to the moment it is resolved and closed, coordinating engineers, operations, customer communications, legal, and security toward the fastest possible restoration of service for customers.
  
  
This is a coordination and leadership role, not a hands on resolver role. You will not perform the technical fix or make specialized safety decisions. You will make sure the right responders are engaged, the severity is assessed correctly, work that crosses team boundaries is sequenced, communication and any regulatory obligations are tracked, and the event ends in learning that prevents recurrence. Your effectiveness is measured by the quality of your coordination under pressure, not by personal troubleshooting. You are calm and diligent in high stress situations, you create urgency and focus, you ask the hard questions, and you can direct senior people who do not report to you.
  
  
Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.
  
  
Key job responsibilities
  
  

* Serve as the single accountable call leader on high severity events, from declaration through resolution and closure.
* Assess and set event severity based on customer and business impact, and adjust it as the event evolves.
* Run the incident bridge, keeping the engineering effort and the customer communication effort aligned on a single source of truth.
* Sequence work across engineering, operations, mission and flight operations, customer communications, legal, and security, and engage the right responders quickly.
* Keep customer communication and any regulatory notification obligations visible and on time, at the same priority as the technical mitigation.
* Escalate early and freely, clear blockers, and make the stand down decision against clear recovery criteria
* Run clean handovers on prolonged events, and share a twenty four by seven on call rotation.
* Proactively investigate early warning signals to catch potential events before they reach customers.
* Own the post event loop, ensuring a correction of errors and root cause analysis are completed, assigned, and tracked to closure.
* Audit the coverage of monitoring and customer notification so events are detected and communications reach the right customers.
* Design, run, and score simulated incident exercises, and train partner teams on the incident process and their role on the call.
* Improve runbooks and incident tooling, reducing the manual work of running an event.

* Experience managing programs across cross functional teams, building processes and coordinating release schedules

* Excellent written and verbal communication, able to produce clear updates for both engineers and executive stakeholders.

**About Anthropic**
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
  
  
**About The Role**
We are looking for an Incident Response Manager to serve as the operational backbone of how Anthropic handles incidents. When things go wrong, you are the person who makes sure the right people are in the room, the right information is flowing, and nothing falls through the cracks.
  
  
The right person for this role brings structure and rigor to high-volume, high-stakes situations without waiting for a playbook to be handed to them. You will work across engineering, product, security, legal, go-to-market, and leadership to ensure Anthropic responds to incidents with speed, clarity, and accountability. This is not a role where you follow existing runbooks; it is a role where you write them, and where you operate effectively even when the runbook does not yet exist.
  
  
**Responsibilities**

* Build the incident response management function, establishing the processes, tooling, and operational standards that define how we handle incidents at scale
* Serve as an on-call incident commander, driving coordinated response across technical and non-technical stakeholders during incidents of varying severity, including managing multiple active incidents simultaneously
* Engage the right people at the right time, with a strong sense of urgency, bringing order and direction to fast-moving, ambiguous situations
* Own incident communications end-to-end, from real-time internal coordination to external channels like status pages, direct customer outreach, and stakeholder updates, ensuring they reflect Anthropic's commitments to safety, transparency, and accuracy
* Participate in blameless incident reviews, contributing operational context and helping drive follow-through on critical remediations so the same class of incident does not recur
* Partner with engineering teams to develop and maintain incident response policies, procedures, and escalation frameworks that scale with Anthropic's growth
* Partner with engineering, product, security, legal, and go-to-market teams to continuously improve how the organization detects, responds to, and learns from incidents

**You May Be a Good Fit If You**

* Have 5+ years of experience in incident management, with direct experience managing technical product or infrastructure incidents (not exclusively security or trust and safety)
* Have built or significantly shaped an incident response program, ideally at a high-growth startup or in an environment where you had to create structure rather than inherit it
* Demonstrate a strong sense of ownership and urgency, with the ability to operate independently and make sound decisions under pressure without waiting for direction
* Are comfortable working in unprecedented situations where processes are still being defined and guidance may be incomplete or conflicting, leaving things better than you found them
* Have a track record of effective cross-functional collaboration, particularly with engineering, security, legal, communications, go-to-market, and executive leadership
* Bring a blameless, learning-oriented mindset to incident reviews, focused on systemic improvement rather than individual fault
* Have experience with cloud infrastructure incidents and enough technical depth across the stack to engage meaningfully with engineering teams during response, including comfort navigating distributed systems, monitoring tools, and logs
* Are analytically minded, with experience using data (incident metrics, queries, trend analysis) to inform decisions during response and to drive operational improvements over time
* Communicate clearly and calmly under pressure, both in real-time coordination and in post-incident written communications
* Thrive in high-volume, fast-paced environments and are energized by bringing operational discipline to complex, evolving situations

**About the Role**
